source_text.slice: REQ-519 slice 2f-a (GH #2535): the on-gate machinery (OnGate, ScopedApprovers, ShadowWindow, RefusedAudit, ShadowEvidence.counts_by_day/3, Audit.latest_matching/4, integrity on_gate block, count_interactive_explicit_tenant_wide_admins/1, flip_actions/flip_resource_type). Tests only; nothing under lib/ or priv/ was changed; nothing committed.

task.description: Write the test spec and test code for REQ-519 slice 2f-a (design r2a section 1 2f-a rows, T-G*, T-P*, T-E*, T-F*, mutants assigned to 2f-a), ACs 7 (2f-a part), 9, 10, 11, 12 (source of the sentence), 14 (writer), 15 (refused), 18 (gate half), the SEC step-16 merge conditions and the REVIEWER step-17 notes. Per-file runs only under the shared mixlock; no mix letflow.check.test, no full or multi-partition suite; mutants applied in memory only.

result.summary: 133 new tests in 7 new files plus one new support module, ALL GREEN, run per file, one mix at a time under the mixlock (MIX_ENV=test): latest_matching 9, on_gate 35, scoped_approvers 18, shadow_window 33, refused_audit 13, dormant_on 16, integrity router 9. The neighbours that 2f-a touched stay green and UNEDITED by this step: scope_enforcement_test 23, routers/tenant_scope_enforcement_test 26, identity/sync_scope_guard_test 40 (the dedup is now served by Audit.latest_matching/4). No compiler warning in any run. mix format was not run as a mix task; each file was instead formatted and checked with Code.format_string! in a plain elixir script (it reports ok for four existing test/support files it was calibrated on) and all new files are unchanged by it. 43 mutants measured in memory: 43 killed, 0 survive; three of them (MU-28, MU-29c, MU-29d) first survived or were unkillable with my first tests and drove test changes (see mutants). NOT RUN by instruction: mix letflow.check.test, full or multi-partition suites (the warnings-as-errors dead-default check of that task was therefore not run; by inspection no helper added in this step has a default argument, and every run printed no compiler warning). The shadow -> on path inside flip/4 is dormant, so the flip-level halves of AC 14/18 and mutants MU-22/MU-23/MU-39/MU-42 (flip half) are not testable in this PR: listed in the spec for 2f-b. No implementation bug found.

mutants.summary: 43 mutants: 43 killed, 0 survive. Three first survived or could not be killed and changed the tests: MU-28 (a rescue around fact 2 survived while the tables were renamed inside a rolled-back transaction, since the aborted transaction makes every later read raise; the rename is now committed DDL restored in an after), MU-29c (the role filter of the group rows; added a tenant-wide group row of ANOTHER role next to the scoped TASK_WORKER row), MU-29d (the routing-kind holder; the test needed a scoped USER row to isolate the binding kind).
mutants.not_measured: MU-22 (S lock order inside on_checks!/3), MU-23 (off -> on allowed), MU-39 (a raised precondition recorded as a refusal), MU-42 flip half (flush dropped from flip/4) and the attrs[:now] clause: all live only on the dormant shadow -> on path of flip/4, unreachable until 2f-b widens parse_mode/@modes/check_target. A mutant that turns the audit_failed branch of RefusedAudit.write/6 into success is not killable: Audit.insert_entry/3 cannot return an error tuple for a valid schema name (it raises, covered by T-F10).

implementation_findings: NO IMPLEMENTATION BUG FOUND: every test is green against the working tree and every mutant is killed.

OBS-1: flip(:on) is :invalid_mode, so the shadow -> on path of flip/4 (flush, on_checks!, refusal audit after the rollback, shadow_required, the one rescue around OnGate.evaluate) is untestable in 2f-a; the dormant_on tests are the proof that nothing opened the door and the spec lists the 2f-b obligations.

OBS-2: DateTime.diff(now, t0, :second) floors EACH operand to whole seconds, so the duration criterion has whole-second resolution (a now 1 microsecond short of t0 + 7 days still passes when both fall in the same second). Harmless for a 7-day gate; the tests use whole-second offsets. Not a defect.

OBS-3: RefusedAudit.write/6 has an audit_failed branch that is unreachable (Audit.insert_entry/3 raises rather than returning an error tuple for a valid prefix); the exception branch is the one a fault produces and is pinned.

OBS-4: integrity/1 reads the grant tables before it derives the tenant id, so the 'invalid tenant schema prefix' ArgumentError is reachable only for a complete schema with a non-tenant name (a bogus schema fails earlier with a Postgres error). Pinned with a renamed fixture schema; harmless (no route supplies such a prefix).

OBS-5: the Elixir 1.20 type checker warns about deliberately wrong arguments even through a function capture; the wrong-argument tests route the value through OnGateFixture.opaque/1 so no compile warning exists.

OBS-6 (SEC F-2, observability): GET /integrity has no rescue and no constant log line when a fact read raises, as SEC noted; this step pins that a raise propagates out of integrity/1 (no partial report) but cannot pin the HTTP 500 shape, which depends on the surrounding plug stack and was not exercised.

OBS-7 (environment): the mixlock directory is also taken by other sessions (owner file); my scripts created it only when absent and removed only a lock they created; scratch scripts (fmt.exs, mut.exs, mutrun.sh, runtests.sh, batch logs) live in the session scratchpad, not in the repository.
